# Step 2.242: the device tells its own commands by their IDs

## Builder 1 (the layers below the screen)

- `packages/sports` not touched. The server's list is beside the engine's state, not in it.
- Server (T-356, pending): `games.read_tracker_state` gives `changes`, the command IDs (lower case) of the changes of players among the last 300 events up to the state's sequence, refused adds included, read through the existing `eventsAfter` (no new query, no migration). With no state saved (changes only), the sequence is now the last change's, as the commands' answer already said. The endpoint gives `changes` only to a tracker sending `X-Tracker-Changes: 1` (`trackerChangesHeader`, contract `TrackerGameStateWithChanges`): an earlier release's strict contract would read the extra list as "not the server's" (T-127). `fetch-tracker-server.ts` sends it; `ServerState.changes` is optional.
- Device (T-357, pending): `commands-since.ts` judges the commands between two states by ID: `own`, `somebody-else`, or `cannot-tell` (the lists name fewer commands than the sequences differ by, a state with no `changes`, a state older than the one known). `carryOnTaps` in `tracker-controller.ts` uses it; own = made, kept on top, stale, everything the storage holds (refused included), `refusedIds`. The old count (`nobodyElseScored`, `ownUnseen`) is gone. On `cannot-tell` the taps are listed as not saved (never sent) and `status.cannotTell` is true until the list empties.
- Spec: T6 §4 (T-318 paragraph) says it. `tracker-controller.test.ts`'s `serverGame` now reads as the tracker does (with `changes`).
- Unit tests (`tracker-controller.test.ts`, describe "step 2.242"; `commands-since.test.ts`, 7 cases; `read-tracker-state.test.ts`, one case). Run on the old controller: (a) refused own add: failed (tap listed); (b) own add taken before the kept state plus another's add: failed (tap sent, 2-2); (d) kept state with no list: failed (tap sent). (c) another's add AND play with own adds: the old code caught it too, so it failed only on the missing `cannotTell`; with the new judge broken by hand (the "not own" check taken out) it and (b) failed. Restored.
- Passed: check, typecheck, vitest of `apps/web/src/features/tracker`, `packages/core/src/modules/games`, `packages/contracts` (117 files, 1356 tests) and `apps/web/src/server` (80 files, 1140), `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs`. Not run: any browser test, `packages/database` (no change there).

In `hold` (`tracker-controller.ts`, the `serially` block that sets `made` and `sessionId = held`): after the rebuild, redraw the screen (`showGame()`) and save the kept scoring, inside the lock; as I read it, nothing is shown or kept until `scoreWith`'s load answers, and a load with no answer leaves the screen and the kept scoring on the old `made`. A unit test failing first (opening answered, `/state` lost).
2. Show `status.cannotTell` on the scoring screen beside the not-saved list (a message in `packages/site/src/messages/en/<area>`, the pinned lists of brief rule 9), and on the phone's short scoreboard if the list is shown there.
3. `tests/browser/bad-wifi-visitors-test.mjs`: put a refused add in the script (an id the server refuses, or a worn number with unique numbers), under the cuts, before a reopen with signal; nothing else may be listed not saved because of it. Ten seeds in a row, printed.
4. Leave the files of lane 2.70 (save a copy, upload) alone.

### What I distrust

- "Send these plays" is not offered (`sendNotSaved: 'none'`) for taps listed from `hold`, the cannot-tell case included: the safe side is "Enter again" only. Offering it there (the server judges, T-335) may be the better "ask"; not changed.
- The read is not under the game's lock: a batch taken between reading the state and the events is cut off by the sequence (the list stops at it), and any mismatch only gives `cannot-tell`, never `own`; argued, not tested against Postgres.
- A state kept before this release has no `changes`: the first reopen after the release with taps of an ended session lists them (`cannot-tell`). Safe, once.

## Builder 2 (the screen, the read under a batch, the browser)

- `hold` (`tracker-controller.ts`): after the rebuild, in the lock, the game is shown (`showGame()`, which keeps the scoring; with no base only the scoring is kept). Unit test "shows the game and keeps the scoring rebuilt in hold, though the state after it is lost": failed first (2-2 shown, kept on top under the ended session), passes now.
- `status.cannotTell` on the screen: `SendNotSaved` (`take-over-parts.tsx`) takes `cannotTell` and says `tracker.sendNotSaved.cannotTell` (in `messages/en/tracker.ts`) beside the not-saved list. One line in `tracker-opening.tsx` (lane 2.70's file) passes it: I had to. The phone's short scoreboard shows only a count, so nothing there.
- "Send these plays" for taps listed because the device could not tell (T-358, pending): offered when it is a first list made under one session; the batch names THAT session (`listedUnder`), not the new one, and the sequence last known. Confirmed in `apply-tracker-commands.ts`: under the game's lock, an ID the server has is answered `duplicate` (`taken`, in `refuseAll` and `applyOne`), so nothing counts twice. Unit test: offered, sent, refused, still listed, entered again once, 2-2.
- What I distrust about it: as far as I can see the server will refuse it (`game-moved`) nearly every time. A session that ended by release is deleted, not kept as lost (`findLost` finds nothing), and the commands that left the device unsure are in the very span `gameMovedSince` checks, and they are not among the plays sent. It is safe, but the button mostly ends in "enter them again". Taking the offer away is one condition in `hold`.
- After a reload the list loses `listedUnder`, and the send names the session held now: it is refused, also safe. Not changed.
- The state read with a batch landing in it (`database-tracker.test.ts`, 3 cases, on the real store): PGlite has one connection, so the batch runs through the real command on the read's own connection, after `findState` or `lastEventSeq` has answered. The read cut at its sequence never names the batch's plays, and the device never judges the other's add as its own; the next read catches it. All pass.
- `bad-wifi-visitors-test`: step 8 "77 Ry Refused" is given a version 7 id (the page's `crypto.randomUUID`, once, by an init script), refused `player-id-taken`, before the reopen with signal. The checks now leave that add's row and refusal out by its id (new mark `data-players-refused-player` in `players-panel.tsx`). At the end nothing waits, the banner says 1 play not saved, the panel names only that add, the kept list is empty and only one row is not applied. Ten seeds in a row passed (1720071906, 719093562, 598901438, 156563313, 2026095745, 1117400546, 299281538, 1243234152, 1403952846, 39449939). No check passes on a timeout.
- Browser, once each: tracker-route, bad-wifi, players-panel, takeover-question, tracker-offline, scoring-trouble (one chunk), score-this-game, scoring-plays, scoring-screen (each alone): all passed.
- Not run: the whole browser chain, `packages/database`. I did not check that the new browser step fails on the old count.

## Independent review (2.242)

Read: the plan line, this note, T-356 to T-358, `commands-since.ts`, `carryOnTaps` and `hold`, the state read and its header, `take-over-parts.tsx`, the new tests. Throwaway tests (not committed) and three hand breaks, all restored.

### High

- H1 `tests/browser/bad-wifi-visitors-test.mjs`: the refused add never reaches the judging it was put there to test. `carryOnTaps` runs only when taps of an ENDED session wait (`tracker-controller.ts` 1494), and every reopen in this script finds the session still the device's (line 582). Proof: with the refused add taken for somebody else's (`...stored, ...refusedIds` taken out of the own set, line 1449) seed 1720071906 passed 27 of 27; with `carryOnTaps` forced to answer `taken` whenever there are stale taps, seeds 719093562, 598901438 and 156563313 passed 27 of 27. So the browser half of the plan's done test passes on the old count and on a broken judge. Only the unit tests guard this step. Fix: a reopen after the session has ended (released, or its lease run out) with taps waiting, and the refused add between the kept state and the reopen.

### Medium

- M1 `tracker-controller.ts` 1505-1518 and T-358: "Send these plays" for cannot-tell taps is safe but almost never works. Sent under `listedUnder` and `madeOn`; the server checks, under the game's lock, account, lost session and `gameMovedSince`, and answers a known ID as a duplicate: I found no way to count a play twice or send it under another person. But a released session is deleted, so `findLost` finds nothing and every send ends `game-moved`. Lane 2.70's change ("an ID in the device's own list counts as its own, whoever recorded it") would NOT make it work here, because `findLost` still fails for a released session; and "whoever recorded it" should keep an account check, since the device's own list includes everything its storage holds. My advice: take the offer away (one condition) until the server can judge a released session; keep "Enter again".
- M2 the same block: `notSavedSince` and `listedUnder` are set before the `judge-again` pass and never cleared by it. If the second pass finds somebody else's command (no longer "cannot tell"), the offer stays. Safe (refused), but the offer no longer matches its reason. No test covers it.

### Low

- L1 `commands-since.ts` 33: a kept state with no `changes` meets a list naming an earlier add by somebody else: the answer is `somebody-else`, not `cannot-tell`. Taps are listed either way, but the screen does not say "could not tell" and nothing is offered. Throwaway test.
- L2 `status.cannotTell` stays true until the list empties: taps listed later for another reason (the game lost) are shown under the "could not tell" sentence.
- L3 the message `tracker.sendNotSaved.cannotTell` (tracker.ts 635) promises "A play is never counted twice". That holds for Send. It does not hold if `forgetNotSaved` fails after a send was taken (`.catch(() => undefined)`, already there in T-335) and the scorekeeper then taps Enter again, which gives a new ID.
- L4 own now includes every ID the storage holds. A second tab of the same device shares that storage, so its commands still in storage count as this tab's own. There is no guard against two tabs. This was already true before this step; the step widens it slightly. Not tested.
- L5 T-338 (line 1825) still judges by counting (`answer.sequence - before > answer.took`). A refused add only causes an extra load there, which is safe.

### Holds

- (1) The judge itself: `since` holds only commands really after `from` (`recent` keeps the last 300 engine commands and never drops one on undo; `changes` covers the last 300 events; `eventsAfter` returns all types in seq order). `since.size === count` therefore means every command is named and is the device's own. No order I tried lets another device's command pass as own. Own judged somebody else's only lists taps; none is lost. (2) Tried by throwaway tests: exactly 300 own, 150 plays and 150 changes, 301 with one out of the window, upper-case IDs. A game with no saved state gets the last change's sequence, which is right (plays always save a state); with neither it gets 0. (3) An old tracker reads the state strictly (`tracker-state-endpoint.test.ts` parses with the strict contract), and the strict contract refuses `changes`. An answer without `changes` gives `cannot-tell`. `no-store`; the worker does not catch the API. A dropped header only means "cannot tell". (4) `hold`: the redraw and the save happen in the lock taps run in. A tap made meanwhile waits for the lock, or brings `judge-again`. None is lost or drawn twice. (7) `packages/sports` and `apps/live-stats`: no change.

### My hand breaks

- Unknown taken as own (`commands-since.ts` 35-36): 3 `commands-since` cases and 2 controller cases failed.
- A refused add taken for somebody else's: the controller case "carries the taps on when its own add was refused" failed. The browser test passed (H1).
